findings.title: CRUD/FLS Violation in ContactPhoneService
findings.explanation: The method queries and updates Contact records without enforcing field‑level security. It reads the Birthdate field and writes to Phone regardless of the caller’s field permissions, allowing users to see or modify data they should not access.
findings.remediation: Add WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED to the SOQL query or use Security.stripInaccessible to filter fields. Before updating, check that the user has edit permission on the Phone field (e.g., using Schema.sObjectType.Contact.fields.Phone.isAccessible()).

findings.title: Record-level sharing bypass in Aura-enabled class
findings.explanation: The class is declared "without sharing" and contains an @AuraEnabled method that returns Case records. Without sharing, record-level sharing rules are ignored, allowing any user with the permission set to view cases they should not have access to.
findings.remediation: Declare the class with "with sharing" or "inherited sharing", or enforce sharing in the query using WITH USER_MODE or a sharing query. This ensures record-level access is respected for all callers.

findings.title: Excessive permissions in Support Agent Tools permission set
findings.explanation: The permission set grants ModifyAllData, ViewAllData, and AuthorApex, which give users full access to all data and the ability to author Apex. This far exceeds the described purpose of only viewing and closing cases, creating a privilege escalation risk for internal users.
findings.remediation: Remove the ModifyAllData, ViewAllData, and AuthorApex permissions from the permission set. Grant only the necessary Case object permissions (Read, Edit, and Delete if needed) and the ApiEnabled permission if required for API access.

findings.title: Guest user can access Contact data via AuraEnabled method
findings.explanation: The class is exposed to a Guest User profile and the AuraEnabled method returns Contact records including Email and Phone. Guest users can invoke this method from the site, allowing unauthenticated access to potentially sensitive data.
findings.remediation: Remove the class from the Guest User profile or restrict the method to authenticated users. Ensure the method runs with sharing and uses WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED or Security.stripInaccessible to limit data exposure.

findings.title: Class runs without sharing, ignoring record-level access
findings.explanation: The class is declared "without sharing", so record-level sharing rules are bypassed. Guest users can read all Contact records that match the query, regardless of sharing settings.
findings.remediation: Declare the class with "with sharing" or use WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED in the SOQL query to enforce sharing rules.

findings.title: Query selects fields without enforcing field-level security
findings.explanation: The SOQL query selects the Name field, which the Guest User profile does not grant read access to, and the query does not use WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED. This violates FLS by potentially exposing fields the user should not see.
findings.remediation: Use WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED or Security.stripInaccessible to enforce field-level security, and query only fields that the user has permission to read.
